name: dcomexec.py - Remote Execution via DCOM
description: dcomexec.py executes commands on remote Windows hosts via DCOM (Distributed Component Object Model) objects like MMC20.Application, ShellWindows, and ShellBrowserWindow. Does not create a service or drop a binary - uses legitimate Windows DCOM interfaces. Less detected than PsExec/smbexec but slower.
notes:
=== BASIC USAGE ===
  dcomexec.py <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<target>
  dcomexec.py <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<target> "whoami"
  dcomexec.py <domain>/<user>@<target> -hashes :<nthash>

=== DCOM OBJECTS ===
  # MMC20.Application (default):
  dcomexec.py -object MMC20 <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<target>
  # ShellWindows:
  dcomexec.py -object ShellWindows <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<target>
  # ShellBrowserWindow:
  dcomexec.py -object ShellBrowserWindow <domain>/<user>:<pass>@<target>

=== PASS THE HASH ===
  dcomexec.py <domain>/<user>@<target> -hashes aad3b435b51404eeaad3b435b51404ee:<nthash>

=== KERBEROS AUTH ===
  export KRB5CCNAME=ticket.ccache
  dcomexec.py -k -no-pass <domain>/<user>@<target>

=== COMPARISON: LATERAL MOVEMENT TOOLS ===
  # psexec.py:    Creates service, writes binary. LOUD. SYSTEM shell.
  # smbexec.py:   Creates service for each command. Moderate noise.
  # wmiexec.py:   Uses WMI. Semi-interactive. Moderate detection.
  # dcomexec.py:  Uses DCOM. No service/binary. Lower detection.
  # atexec.py:    Uses Task Scheduler. Single command. Moderate.
  # evil-winrm:   Uses WinRM (port 5985). Interactive. Common.

recommended.note: Overview of all Impacket execution tools (psexec, smbexec, wmiexec, atexec).

defense.why_it_works: DCOM objects like MMC20.Application expose ExecuteShellCommand methods that can be called remotely with valid credentials. No service or binary is created on the target.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials with local admin on target; DCOM enabled (default).
defense.impact: Remote command execution; interactive shell on the target.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1021.003] DCOM object instantiation from remote IP; svchost.exe spawning cmd.exe via DcomLaunch; Event 4624 type 3.
defense.artifacts: DCOM-related process creation (mmc.exe, explorer.exe); Event 4624 network logon; child processes from svchost DcomLaunch.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=windows EventCode=4688 ParentProcessName="*svchost.exe*" (NewProcessName="*cmd.exe" OR NewProcessName="*powershell.exe")
| where ParentCommandLine="*DcomLaunch*"
| table _time, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
defense.elastic_kql: process.parent.name:"svchost.exe" AND process.parent.args:"DcomLaunch" AND process.name:("cmd.exe" OR "powershell.exe")
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName == "svchost.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "DcomLaunch"
| where FileName in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Disable remote DCOM when not needed; restrict local admin access; monitor DCOM object instantiation; use Windows Firewall to block DCOM ports from untrusted hosts.

detections.name: DCOM lateral movement - DcomLaunch child process
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName == "svchost.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "DcomLaunch"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "mmc.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Legitimate remote DCOM administration; MMC snap-in usage
detections.tuning: Correlate with network logon (4624 type 3) from unusual source IPs
